Which of the given formulas of PL is the best symbolization of the following sentence?
Doctors are helpful unless their patients are rude.
model_reasoning:
Let H represent 'Doctors are helpful' and R represent 'Their patients are rude'. The word 'unless' in propositional logic is typically translated as an inclusive 'or'. 'P unless Q' means 'P or Q' (P ∨ Q), which is logically equivalent to 'If not Q then P' (~Q → P). Applying this to the sentence 'Doctors are helpful unless their patients are rude', we get 'H unless R'. This translates to H ∨ R (Doctors are helpful or their patients are rude) or equivalently ~R → H (If their patients are not rude, then doctors are helpful). Comparing this with the given choices:

B) H • R (H and R) - Incorrect.

D) H ∨ R (H or R) - This correctly symbolizes 'H unless R' as it is equivalent to ~R → H (If their patients are not rude, then doctors are helpful).
